details:
Sorry if this was already implemented, but last time I tried to do this, it didn't work. I haven't attempted to do this again recently so I'm not sure if this was implemented or not. The reason why I wanted to do this was to make the fire selector lever on my avatar's gun able to be interacted with by using a custom tag for myself only and for the fingers on everyone else. This is so I can interact with the selector using a very specifically shaped and sized contact on the tip of my finger so I don't "fat finger" the selector (default finger contact size is massive and covers half the gun's receiver and also doesn't always perfectly line up with the finger itself). I still wanted other players to be able to interact with it even if they can't do so efficiently because I've had people come up to play with the gun and get bummed out because they couldn't interact with everything on it like I can. 

I know I could use separate parameters and transition conditions for each contact to make it work, but I feel like it would be better performance-wise to only need one. 

When I tried to do this, the parameter wouldn't update correctly, presumably because one contact is being triggered and one isn't, causing the parameter to receive both true and false at the same time. Ideally, if one contact is triggered, parameter should favor that one and update the parameter accordingly. 

For example:

one true + any others false = true

all false = false

all true = true

Another neat idea I'll add here while I'm thinking about it is the ability to use a float to take the number of contacts triggered as a decimal. 

So if you have 4 and 1 is triggered, 0.25. 

I bet there's some fun stuff you could do with that as well. 

Thanks for reading and considering this idea!
title: Allow multiple contact receivers to use same parameter
